steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Social stratification: the hierarchical arrangement of people into social strata based on wealth, income, status and power. In the UK, social class is the primary form of stratification. | Key Fact: Social class systems: the NS-SEC (8 classes from higher managerial to never worked) replaced the Registrar General's scale. Weber: class is based on market situation. Marx: class is based on relationship to means of production. | Key Fact: Life chances: class strongly affects health (working-class die 7-9 years earlier), education (middle-class children achieve higher), income (top 10% earn 12x more than bottom 10%), and housing (overcrowding 5x higher in lowest quintile). | Key Fact: The wealth gap: richest 10% hold 44% of total wealth; poorest 50% hold 9%.
